item.title: Trump: US Won't Attack Iran Before Midterm Elections
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says Iran could take advantage militarily and economically of President Trump's announcement that the US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections. Brett Bruen, President of the Global Situation Room and former US diplomat, says Iran may not go along with President Trump's effort to keep tensions down before the midterm elections and could continue using attacks to demonstrate its leverage. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Debrief with Mario Parker: Tight Race Republicans Confront Trump Dilemma
item.description: Bloomberg's Mario Parker joins to discuss Republican candidates distancing themselves from President Trump in key races and strategists' concerns about his approval rating for The Debrief. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bruen: Political Power Is Diffusing in Post-American Era
item.description: Brett Bruen, President of the Global Situation Room and former US diplomat, says Iran may not go along with President Trump's effort to keep tensions down before the midterm elections and could continue using attacks to demonstrate its leverage. Bruen says President Trump cannot speak on behalf of Israel and says Netanyahu will make his own calculations based in part on his political prospects. Bruen says leaders in Europe, Canada, Japan and the Middle East are starting to build their own structures as political power diffuses in what he calls a "post-American era," creating a new economic and political dynamic. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Krishnamoorthi: This War Is a Disaster
item.description: Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) says Iran could take advantage militarily and economically of President Trump's announcement that the US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections. Rep. Krishnamoorthi says he doesn't put much stock in President Trump's claim that the US is having productive discussions with Iran and says the conflict is benefiting China and Russia by drawing US forces and munitions toward the Middle East. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Trade Worries, Oil & Treasury Yields Pressure Markets
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Schroders Head of US Fixed Income Neil Sutherland, Applied Digital Founder & CEO Wes Cummins, Barclays Managing Director & US Equity Research Analyst Lauren Lieberman, Siebert Williams Shank President, CEO, and Co-Founder Suzanne Shank, Citi Research Analyst Jon Tower, 248 Ventures Chief Investment Strategist Lindsey Bell, Arc’teryx CEO Stuart Haselden, Patagonia CEO Ryan Gellert, True Religion Apparel CEO Michael Buckley, BTIG Managing Director, Consumer Equity Research Janine Stichter, & Cowboy Space Founder & CEO Baiju Bhatt. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mamdani Says Child Was in Car When ICE Shot Man in New York
item.description: A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent shot and wounded a man in New York City on Thursday, prompting Mayor Zohran Mamdani to demand an end to ICE operations in the city.
item.dc:creator: Myles Miller

item.title: Why Trump Suspended Microsoft and Other Tech Firms From a Green Card Program
item.description: From the start of his second term, President Donald Trump has made it a top priority to restrict opportunities for non-Americans to gain entry or remain in the US. In the latest action on that front, his administration said on Oct. 8 that it would indefinitely suspend the ability of a number of technology companies, including Microsoft Corp., to sponsor foreign employees for permanent residency in the US.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Kreighbaum

item.title: Hegseth Vows Public Firing-Squad Execution for Fort Hood Shooter
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the firing-squad execution of Nidal Hasan, a former Army major who killed 13 people in a mass shooting in 2009, would be visible to the public.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Milligan

item.title: Most French View Bardella Allegations With Concern in Ifop Poll
item.description: A large majority of French say alleged antisemitic comments made by Jordan Bardella, the head of the far-right National Rally, would be a serious matter if proven true, according to an opinion poll.
item.dc:creator: Albertina Torsoli

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Iran Strikes Delayed (Podcast)
item.description: The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF. President Donald Trump said the US would not attack Iran ahead of November’s midterm elections, citing “productive discussions” with the Islamic Republic. Trump's comments came despite Iran ramping up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Tehran-backed militants in Yemen attacking energy facilities in Saudi Arabia. The US will keep a naval blockade of Iranian exports in place, and recently moved its B-1B bombers from a base in the United Kingdom due to possible Iran-linked threats. The remarks follow recent reporting in The Atlantic that Trump was mulling plans to strike Iran before the midterm contests and that the White House had asked the Pentagon to prepare options for strikes beforehand. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fight for Senate Control Moves to Debate Stage in Key Battlegrounds
item.description: Candidates in Georgia, Michigan and Maine will face off in the high-stakes forums.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Lucey

item.title: US Suspends Visa Program for Tech Firms, Mideast Fighting Spurs Inflation Fears
item.description: The Trump administration is launching investigations into the use of foreign exchange visa programs at nine top colleges including Harvard, Stanford, and MIT, in its latest broadside against international students and scholars at elite schools. We speak with Bloomberg's Mike Shepard in Washington. Oil surged as fresh tanker attacks by Iran threaten to curtail a recent uptick in flows from the Middle East, as President Trump said the US would not attack Iran ahead of November’s midterm elections. Ellen Wald of Transversal Consulting joins for a closer look. We examine the state of the American labor market and the outlook for Fed policy with Claudia Sahm, Chief Economist at New Century Advisors. Plus - youth flag football participation has soared in an almost impossibly short time, especially among girls. Bloomberg's Amanda Mull joins to explain. All on the latest episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Judge Sides With Importers to Expand Trump Tariff Refund Fight
item.description: A US trade judge approved class-action status for a legal fight over refunds for President Donald Trump’s global tariffs, siding with importers who contend that the process will make it easier for a wider group of companies to get their money back.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman

item.title: US Suspends Visa Program for Tech Firms Including Microsoft
item.description: Bloomberg's Wendy Benjaminson said that President Trump is balancing shoring up support from tech firms for his vision of an AI future with a base that remains anti-immigration, as the Trump administration suspends an immigration program for multiple tech firms including Microsoft. Benjaminson also discussed President Trump's announcement on Truth Social that the US would not be striking Iran until after the midterm elections, saying that even without strikes voters aren't going to forget the impact of war with Iran on affordability. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: France to Fight Student Unrest by Sending Thousands of Teachers
item.description: France’s government pledged to dispatch thousands of additional teachers to understaffed schools throughout the country in an effort to rein in student protests that have led to clashes with riot police.
item.dc:creator: Albertina Torsoli

item.title: Trump Says US Won’t Attack Iran Before Midterm Elections
item.description: President Donald Trump said in a social media post that the US would “not be attacking Iran” before November’s midterm elections, citing what he said were “productive discussions” with the Islamic Republic.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Ellen Milligan

item.title: Harvard, MIT Face Visa Probes Amid US Crackdown on Global Talent
item.description: The Trump administration is launching investigations into the use of foreign exchange visa programs at nine top colleges including Harvard University, Stanford University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, in its latest broadside against international students and scholars at elite schools.
item.dc:creator: Liam Knox

item.title: US Bars Microsoft, Indian Firms From Visa Program in Blow
item.description: The Trump administration accused Microsoft Corp., Adobe Inc. and a half-dozen other companies of abusing a US worker visa program and suspended them indefinitely from a longstanding immigration initiative that’s served as a crucial talent pipeline for Silicon Valley and Wall Street.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Matt Day and Alicia A. Caldwell

item.title: Hochstein Says Republican Midterm Weakness Tied to War
item.description: An adviser to former President Joe Biden said the Iran war is a significant vulnerability for Republicans and cast doubt on the political logic of escalating the conflict before the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Ari Natter, Annmarie Hordern, Jonathan Ferro and Lisa Abramowicz

item.title: Trump Builds Latin America Military Alliance on the Cheap
item.description: Donald Trump has slashed US aid to Latin America even as country after country has elected governments aligned with him.
item.dc:creator: Maya Averbuch
